bib.title: Large Language Models Are Human-Level Prompt Engineers

read.skipped: Figure-axis residue after Fig 28 (extra iterative-search plots, Figs 29-32+) is numbers only; figure data not recoverable from text.

question: Can an LLM automatically generate and select natural-language instructions that match or beat human-written prompts, treating instruction writing as black-box program synthesis?
hypothesis: Searching a pool of LLM-proposed instructions with a score function over demonstrations yields instructions as good as those of human prompt engineers; softer log-prob scores and iterative resampling might help.
contributions: Frame instruction generation as natural language program synthesis, formulate it as black-box optimization guided by LLMs, and propose naive and iterative Monte Carlo search.
APE achieves human-level zero-shot performance with model-generated instructions on 24/24 Instruction Induction and 17/21 BIG-Bench tasks.
Extensive qualitative and quantitative analyses, with applications to few-shot learning, zero-shot chain of thought, and steering toward truthfulness/informativeness.

method.summary: APE samples candidate instructions from an LLM given 5 input-output demonstrations (forward or infilling 'reverse' templates), scores each on a target LLM (execution accuracy or log-prob of the answer) using adaptive multi-stage subset evaluation, and returns the top-scoring instruction. An optional iterative variant resamples semantically similar variants of top candidates. Nothing is trained; the selected instruction is evaluated zero-shot (or prepended to few-shot prompts) on InstructGPT.

inference.max_tokens: instruction generation capped at a predefined 50 tokens (Fig 11 caption)
inference.samples: default 50 sampled instruction candidates per task (Sec 5.2); 5 runs with different random seeds, mean and std reported for instruction induction; 250 instructions per model for the proposal-quality study, scored on 50 test points; 200 candidates for TruthfulQA, top 10 on train kept; 250 instructions per task scored on 10 test points for score-function correlation
inference.prompting: 5 input-output demonstrations in the proposal prompt; zero-shot evaluation template 'Instruction: [INSTRUCTION]\nInput: [ ]\nOutput:'; few-shot evaluation places instruction before in-context demonstrations

parameters.iterative_APE: resampling prompt; gains level off after about 3 rounds
parameters.efficient_score_estimation: multi-stage: evaluate all candidates on small subset, candidates above a threshold get new non-overlapping subsets with moving-average score, until a small set is evaluated on full training set; top-k% fraction and threshold not stated
parameters.sample_size_curve: 4 to 128 samples; human level reached at 64
parameters.cot_search: answer prefix constrained to start with "Let's", scored by likelihood of filtered correct reasoning chains

other.hyperparameter_note: Appendix F: number of proposals per demonstration and demonstrations per seed were retuned; 5 tasks re-evaluated to reach 24/24 (previous version 19/24); values not given

metrics.name: execution accuracy
metrics.definition: 0-1 loss 1[M([rho;Q])=A]; some tasks use invariants (e.g. order-invariant set matching)

metrics.name: interquartile mean (IQM)
metrics.definition: IQM of zero-shot execution accuracy across 24 tasks (Agarwal et al. 2021)

metrics.name: normalized preferred metric (BBII)
metrics.definition: 100 = human expert, 0 = random; can go below 0

metrics.name: % True / % Info / % True+% Info
metrics.definition: fine-tuned GPT-judge and GPT-info automated metrics of Lin et al. 2022

baselines: Human prompt engineers (gold annotations of Honovich et al. 2022; default BIG-Bench human prompt; 'help' prompt of Lin et al. 2022; human CoT triggers)
Greedy (Honovich et al. 2022 model-generated instruction, no search)
eval.protocol: Instructions selected on train demonstrations, scored on held-out test set; instruction induction repeated over 5 seeds (mean, std); no significance tests; TruthfulQA is not true few-shot because instructions are tuned on 100 train items.

results.quote: achieves equal or better than human performance on 24 of 24 tasks

results.claim: IQM across 24 tasks: APE vs human.
results.quote: obtaining an IQM of 0.810 vs humans’ 0.749

results.claim: APE CoT trigger improves MultiArith over 'Let's think step by step'.
results.setup: text-davinci-002, zero-shot CoT, answer prefix constrained to start with "Let's", scored by likelihood of filtered correct reasoning chains
results.quote: This generated prompt further improves performance from 78.7 to 82.0 on MultiArith and from 40.7 to 43.0 on GSM8K.

limits: Instructions are tuned on the evaluation data (TruthfulQA): not true few-shot, not comparable with the original benchmark.
Instructions overfit the scorer: Rhymes echo-the-input hack; instructions transfer poorly to a different model.
Iterative search gives only marginal gain; meta-prompt template matters and is left to future work.
Instruction generation and scoring costs more offline than in-context learning, amortised only over many inferences.
Decoding temperature, top-k% filter and score thresholds are not stated; model identity assumed (footnote 3).
Human baseline for TruthfulQA is not carefully chosen (Askell et al. 2021) so the win is not surprising; CoT trigger found hard to optimise on Shuffled Objects and Last Letter.
Only OpenAI API models of 2022 vintage; everything depends on proprietary models that have since been retired.
